questions.question: India has an open border with which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal**__

__
 
• India shares an **open border** with **Nepal**.
 
• This means that the movement of people between the two countries is largely unrestricted.
 
• The open border facilitates trade, commerce, and cultural exchange between India and Nepal.
 
• **Citizens of both countries can travel without the need for a visa or passport**, adhering to certain identification requirements.
 
• The open border agreement is a significant aspect of the friendly and cooperative relationship between India and Nepal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The India-Nepal open border is established under the **1950 Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship**.
 
• The treaty allows for free movement of people and goods between the two nations and grants reciprocal rights of residence, ownership of property, participation in trade and commerce, and other privileges.
 
• This open border has historical significance and has been in place for decades, reflecting the deep-rooted ties between the two countries.
 
• Despite the open border, both nations have established mechanisms to address security concerns and manage cross-border activities effectively.
 
• The open border is a unique feature of India-Nepal relations and is not common with India's other neighboring countries.

• **Article 25-28** of the Indian Constitution deal with the '**Right to Freedom of Religion**'.
 
• These articles ensure that all individuals have the freedom to profess, practice, and propagate their religion.
 
• The provisions under these articles also protect religious practices and allow religious groups to manage their own affairs in matters of religion.
 
• Article 25 guarantees **freedom of conscience** and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• Article 26 ensures the** freedom to manage religious affairs**.
 
• Article 27 provides **freedom from payment of taxes **for promotion of any particular religion.
 
• Article 28 allows **freedom from attending religious **instruction or worship in certain educational institutions.

• The **Right to Freedom of Religion** is a fundamental right under **Part III** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rights are subject to public order, morality, and health, and to other provisions of Part III of the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution of India aims to maintain a balance between the freedom of religion and other fundamental rights to ensure harmony and peace in the society.
 
• India is a secular state, which means that the state treats all religions impartially and does not uphold any religion as the state religion.

• It is the longest written constitution of any country in the world and lays down the framework for political principles, government structure, and the rights and duties of citizens.

questions.question: _________ dance form originates from the southern Indian state of Kerala.

__
 
• **Kathakali and Mohiniyattam** are traditional dance forms that **originate from Kerala**, a state in southern India.
 
• **Kathakali** is known for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and face masks, and it typically depicts stories from Hindu epics and mythology.
 
• **Mohiniyattam**, which translates to "**dance of the enchantress**," is characterized by graceful, swaying body movements and subtle facial expressions.
 
• Both dance forms are integral to Kerala's cultural heritage and have a significant place in Indian classical dance traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 25 percent more than its cost price. What is the maximum discount percentage at which the shopkeeper sells his article with no profit or no loss?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of CP : MP = 100 : 125 = 4 : 5.

For no profit/loss, SP must be equal to CP, so SP = 4 units.

Discount allowed = MP − SP = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup % = 25%

Condition = No profit or loss (SP = CP)

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31c759cfa518c1f3afcfa8836f55064a51b00845abf53d14b1ab802049e9db75.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) of the article = ₹100

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = CP + 25% of CP = 100 + 25 = ₹125

⇒ Since there is no profit and no loss, Selling Price (SP) = CP = ₹100

⇒ Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price

⇒ Discount = 125 − 100 = ₹25

⇒ Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (25 ÷ 125) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 1/5 × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Markup Percentage

Markup % is the percentage by which the CP is increased to get the MP. MP = CP × [1 + (Markup% ÷ 100)].

Relationship between Markup, Discount and Profit

Net Profit% = Markup% − Discount% − [(Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100]. If Profit = 0, then Markup% − Discount% = (Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP × [1 − (Discount% ÷ 100)].
